summary: Weighing Sukamal Banerjee's DET margin rebound (14.2% EBIT), Cyient Semi (+240.8% YoY), and DLM's 1.6x+ book-to-bill against ₹2,759 Cr debt, 119-day CCC, and 8.61% ROE yields a probability-weighted expected value of ₹1,232.50 (+11.5% vs CMP ₹1,104.90). New capital is assigned WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (entry zone ₹1,027.29–₹1,058.57, stop ₹951.20, 2.06:1 support R:R vs 1.14:1 at CMP). Existing Zerodha holdings (91 shares, ₹1,00,545.90, 2.34% weight) are assigned HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP at ₹951.20, while marginal cash stays 100% in CASH.

web_blocks.html: We now synthesize the price-blind business audit (Chapters 1–6), Reverse DCF and peer valuation (Chapter 7), and Stage 2 multi-timeframe tape (Chapter 8) into a single, non-hedged investment decision. Because Cyient is both an active portfolio holding and a fresh-capital underwriting candidate, we derive the New Capital Verdict and the Current Holding Action independently from the same evidence [27].

web_blocks.caption: Both Sides of the Aisle: Bull Steelman vs. Bear / Skeptic Steelman
headers: The Bear / Skeptic Case (How It Breaks)
rows: Core DET Turnaround
Under CEO Sukamal Banerjee, Q2 FY27 DET revenue grew +15.7% YoY (+9.3% organic) and EBIT margin hit a 10-quarter high of 14.2%, proving the FY25 guidance shock is behind it [3].
Organic growth still relies on cyclical aerospace/rail capex; margin expansion partly reflects restructuring and one-time cost cuts that may plateau near 14–15% [1][3].
DET stabilization is real, but sustainability over 4+ quarters—especially in Connectivity—must be verified.
M&A & Semicon Pivot
Kinetic Technologies ($85M) + TAO Digital ($218M) transform Cyient into a high-growth AI data engineering and custom ASIC platform (+240.8% YoY Semi growth) [6][7].
Borrowings jumped 6.4x to ₹2,759 Cr in 6 months, Fixed Assets/intangibles doubled to ₹6,021 Cr, and Q2 interest rose to ₹37 Cr with 33–36% tax rates [1].
High-upside strategic pivot, but balance-sheet cushion is gone; execution errors now carry financial leverage risk.
Cash Flow & DLM
FY26 CFO was ₹787 Cr (118% CFO/EBITDA) and FCF was ₹693 Cr; DLM carries a 1.6x+ book-to-bill with Boeing/defense programs [1][13][14].
Inventory Days hit 303 and CCC stretched to 119 days; ROCE compressed to 12.3% and trailing ROE is 8.61% [1].
Receivables are clean (66 days), but DLM inventory and M&A integration demand strict working-capital discipline.
Valuation & Tape
Above rising 30W SMA (₹974.01) and 200D SMA (₹964.04); ~21.7x–22.5x normalized FY28E EPS (₹49–51); DIIs hold 38.96% [1][20].
Ledger classifies Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) below 50D SMA (₹1,120.11) with 4 dist. days; CMP R:R is 1.14:1 and 4H chart is weak [20][27].
Do not chase at CMP; require ₹1,027.29–₹1,058.57 support, 4H/50-DMA reclaim, and Q3 debt <₹2,500 Cr.
web_blocks.takeaway: Cyient is a credible Stage 2 turnaround, not an unconditional compounder. Patience on new entries and a hard stop on existing shares balance upside participation against leverage risk.

web_blocks.caption: Probability-Weighted 12–18 Month Scenario Outcomes (CMP: ₹1,104.90)
rows: Bull Case
DET EBIT >15%, Cyient Semi scales past $100M run-rate, TAO Digital accretive in Year 1, stock re-rates to 30x FY28E EPS.
Base Case
DET holds 14%+ EBIT, FY28E EPS recovers to ₹49–51 at 25.5x P/E, borrowings gradually pay down below ₹1,800 Cr.
Bear Case
TAO/Kinetic integration stalls, DLM CCC stays >120 days, interest + tax drag keeps EPS <₹38, multiple compresses to 21x.
Probability-Weighted Expected Value
Positive expected value, but CMP R:R (1.14:1) is below our 1.50:1 hurdle; Support-Zone R:R (at ₹1,058.57) is 2.06:1.
web_blocks.takeaway: Probability-weighted expected return (+11.5%) does not clear our hurdle at ₹1,104.90, but improves sharply to 2.06:1 reward-to-risk inside the ₹1,027.29–₹1,058.57 support zone.

web_blocks.caption: Multi-Horizon Investment Judgment (New Capital Verdict: WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT)
rows: Short-Term (1–3 Months)
Wait for 4H Turn & Support
Ledger is Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) below 50D SMA (₹1,120.11), and 4H RSI (47.21) sits below 4H EMA20 (₹1,114.25). Require support at ₹1,027.29–₹1,058.57 plus 4H/50-DMA reclaim.
Medium-Term (6–18 Months)
Conditional Inflection
Mandatory prerequisite: Q3/Q4 FY27 filings must prove borrowings step down below ₹2,500 Cr, interest peaks, and TAO Digital / Kinetic integrate cleanly.
Long-Term (3–5 Years)
Conditional Compounder
Aerospace/rail ER&D + custom ASICs + AI data engineering is a powerful mix, but ROCE must recover from 12.3% back above 16–18% to earn CORE_ALPHA status.
web_blocks.takeaway: New capital is gated at WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT until price tests ₹1,027.29–₹1,058.57 AND confirms both a 4H/50-DMA trend reclaim and Q3 FY27 deleveraging (<₹2,500 Cr borrowings).

book_paragraphs: We have reached the moment of synthesis. Across eight chapters, you and I have stripped away the market noise, audited Cyient's 10-year financial record blind to the stock price, uncovered the ₹2,328 crore debt surge behind the Kinetic Technologies and TAO Digital deals, tested the ₹1,104.90 share price against a Reverse DCF and five listed peers, and mapped the Stage 2 weekly and 4-hour charts. Now it is time to make an explicit, non-hedged decision for both fresh money and the shares you already own.

Let us put both sides of the aisle on the table with complete honesty. The Bull case is compelling: new CEO Sukamal Banerjee has already halted the margin bleed in Cyient's core Digital, Engineering & Technology business, driving Q2 FY27 DET revenue up 15.7% year-over-year and lifting EBIT margins to a 10-quarter high of 14.2%. Meanwhile, Cyient Semiconductors grew 240.8% year-over-year and raised $30 million from Edelweiss at a $500 million equity valuation, Cyient DLM is sitting on a 1.6x+ book-to-bill ratio with Boeing and defense programs, and the TAO Digital acquisition adds $115M+ of AI and data engineering scale. If those pieces click together, normalized FY28E earnings per share can recover to ₹49–51, making today's price look like ~22x forward earnings.

The Bear case is equally concrete and cannot be waved away. In a single six-month stretch, Cyient's management spent ₹720 crore on a buyback while taking on ₹2,328 crore of incremental borrowings—pushing total debt from ₹431 crore in March 2026 to ₹2,759 crore in September 2026—and nearly doubled Fixed Assets and intangibles to ₹6,021 crore. Quarterly interest expense has already jumped from ₹14 crore to ₹37 crore, tax rates have climbed to 33–36%, consolidated ROCE sits at just 12.3%, trailing ROE is 8.61%, and Cyient DLM's inventory has stretched the Cash Conversion Cycle to 119 days. If TAO Digital or Kinetic stumbles in integration, equity holders will feel the full force of financial leverage.

When we weight those outcomes—25% Bear at ₹820, 50% Base at ₹1,280, and 25% Bull at ₹1,550—we get a 12-to-18 month probability-weighted expected value of ₹1,232.50, or +11.5% above the 13 November 2026 close of ₹1,104.90. Look at the reward-to-risk math from today's price against our structural invalidation stop at ₹951.20: you are risking ₹153.70 per share to make ₹175.10 in the Base Case—a mediocre 1.14-to-1 ratio. However, if the stock pulls back into the ₹1,027.29 to ₹1,058.57 support zone (centered on Pivot S1 at ₹1,042.93), your risk drops to ₹107.37 while your upside to ₹1,280 rises to ₹221.43—a clean 2.06-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio.

That math dictates our New Capital Verdict: WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. We do not chase Cyient at ₹1,104.90 while the 4-hour chart is still below its 20-period EMA and the business quality verdict is CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL. Instead, we wait patiently for either a confirmed 4-hour turn inside the ₹1,027.29–₹1,058.57 support zone, or Q3 FY27 results confirming that net debt is declining and DET margins are holding above 14%.

What about your existing position? According to the verified 13 November 2026 Zerodha ledger, you hold exactly 91 shares of Cyient at an average cost of ₹1,114.11 (₹1,01,383.80 cost basis), worth ₹1,00,545.90 today—a modest 2.34% weight in your ₹42,97,450.80 Indian net worth, sitting near breakeven (-₹837.90). Because the primary weekly Stage 2 trend is still intact above the rising 30-week SMA (₹974.01) and the position is well-sized at 2.34%, selling into a low-volume consolidation would be premature. Our Holding Action is HOLD_WITH_HARD_STOP: keep all 91 shares today (0 shares to sell now), set a hard structural exit alert if Cyient closes below ₹951.20, monitor the ₹1,058.57 support shelf for potential post-Q3 re-underwriting, and plan to trim 45 shares if the stock rallies into ₹1,280.00 without visible debt reduction.

Finally, where should the next marginal ₹1,00,000 of cash go? Nowhere in a rush. Our 100%-reconciled redeployment table keeps 100% in CASH today. While shortlist candidate Manorama Industries (CMP ₹1,984.10, Base Target ₹2,650.00, 1.68:1 asymmetry) is an attractive ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP candidate and outside peer LTTS (CMP ₹4,247.20) is a quality ER&D benchmark, retaining cash until Cyient's 4-hour turn or a higher-conviction shortlist pullback clears our gates is the highest-discipline choice.

book_subsections.title: Risk-Unit Sizing, Exact Price Alerts & Why We Keep 100% of Marginal Cash Ready
paragraphs: Let us translate our verdict into exact numbers you can act on without second-guessing. Why does our New Capital Verdict say WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT instead of IMMEDIATE_BUY, even though the automated Stage 2 scanner shows CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION? Because an automated technical screen does not know that Cyient's borrowings jumped 6.4x to ₹2,759 crore in September 2026, nor does it enforce a 1.50:1 reward-to-risk hurdle against our fundamental Base Case target of ₹1,280.00.

Look at the exact math from the 13 November 2026 close of ₹1,104.90. Against our structural invalidation stop at ₹951.20, a buyer today risks ₹153.70 per share (-13.91%) to capture ₹175.10 per share (+15.85%) to our ₹1,280.00 Base Case target—a 1.14:1 reward-to-risk ratio. That is below our institutional 1.50:1 minimum hurdle. By contrast, waiting patiently for a pullback into the ₹1,027.29–₹1,058.57 support zone (centered on Pivot S1 at ₹1,042.93) shrinks your downside risk at the top of the band to ₹107.37 (-10.14%) while expanding your upside to ₹221.43 (+20.92%), delivering a clean 2.06:1 reward-to-risk ratio.

At the same time, you already own 91 shares of Cyient in Zerodha at an average cost of ₹1,114.11 (₹1,00,545.90 market value, 2.34% of your ₹42,97,450.80 Indian net worth). Because the stock is in Week 12 of a confirmed Stage 2 uptrend above its rising 30-week SMA (₹974.01) and your position size is a disciplined 2.34%, there is no reason to panic-sell at a tiny -0.83% unrealized loss. Instead, we hold all 91 shares with three explicit, non-emotional alerts: (1) exit all 91 shares if Cyient closes below ₹951.20; (2) re-underwrite for a potential add only if price holds ₹1,027.29–₹1,058.57 with a confirmed 4-hour EMA20 (₹1,114.25) reclaim and Q3 FY27 debt reduction; and (3) trim 45 shares into strength if the stock rallies to ₹1,280.00 without visible deleveraging.

And what about our 100%-reconciled redeployment plan for the next marginal ₹1,00,000 of cash? Today, 100% stays in CASH. Shortlist candidate Manorama Industries (CMP ₹1,984.10, Base Target ₹2,650.00, 1.68:1 asymmetry, ACCUMULATE_ON_DIP) and outside ER&D benchmark LTTS (CMP ₹4,247.20, Base Target ₹4,750.00, 0.64:1 asymmetry) both remain at 0% allocation until either Cyient confirms its support turn or a higher-conviction shortlist pullback triggers.

Let us close with a clear checklist of what will change our mind—both upward and downward—over the next two quarters. Three milestones would upgrade Cyient from WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT to an active accumulation or CORE_ALPHA candidate: first, Q3 FY27 consolidated borrowings stepping down below ₹2,500 crore while quarterly interest expense stabilizes; second, DET sustaining 14.0%+ EBIT margins for two consecutive quarters alongside full-quarter TAO Digital integration without client churn; and third, Cyient DLM reducing its 303-day inventory pile so consolidated Cash Conversion Cycle moves back under 90 days.

Conversely, three red flags would trigger an immediate exit or permanent discard: first, a daily close below ₹951.20 breaking the 30-week SMA; second, DET EBIT margins slipping back below 12.5%; or third, further debt-funded M&A before the Kinetic Technologies and TAO Digital acquisitions have proven their return on invested capital. Stick to the levels, let the tape confirm the turn, and never compromise on reward-to-risk.

Remember why we do this work in two separate passes—price-blind business forensics first, and valuation plus tape second. Had we looked only at the +26.27% three-month rally and Week 12 Stage 2 label, it would have been easy to chase ₹1,104.90 on momentum alone. Had we looked only at the ₹2,759 crore debt jump and 8.61% trailing ROE, it would have been just as easy to dump our 91 Zerodha shares at a tiny loss right before DET's 14.2% margin recovery and Cyient Semiconductors' +240.8% growth bore fruit. By holding both truths at once—keeping our 2.34% position protected by a hard ₹951.20 stop while demanding the ₹1,027.29–₹1,058.57 support zone (2.06:1 R:R) for any fresh rupee—you let the evidence, not emotion, run your portfolio.
